metadata.title: Drying of concrete cylinder — Bažant-Najjar moisture transport validation

source.journal: Portland Cement Association Research Department Bulletin
source.cited_in: Bažant & Najjar (1972), Mat. & Struct. 5:3–20; and Pesavento et al., Chapter 7, Sec. 7.3.4.1, Fig. 7.5, RILEM SOA 27, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-76617-1_7

metadata.validation_method: comparison with relative humidity profile across cylinder diameter at t=7 days after drying start
metadata.validation_target: Radial RH profile h(r) at t=7 days, ambient RH=0.5 (Fig. 7.5)
metadata.notes: Pure moisture transport — no temperature, no hydration, no mechanics. The best-fit parameters from Chapter 7 (C1, a0, hc, N) are explicitly stated and are PAPER_VALUE. Cylinder is mature at start of drying (7 days old) → self-desiccation source hs is neglected (hydration essentially complete). Cylinder length not stated → 2D axisymmetric approximation modelled as 2D rectangle (half cross-section, r=0 to r=R). The pipeline uses Cartesian geometry; a 2D rectangle of half-width R and unit length (or thin strip) exploits symmetry at x=0.

geometry._comment: STRATEGY: Model the half cross-section as a 2D rectangle [0, R] × [0, L_strip]. R = 0.0762 m (3 inches = half-diameter of 6-inch cylinder). L_strip = 0.01 m (thin nominal length — moisture transport is purely radial, L has no effect). The left face x=0 is the axis of symmetry (zero-flux Neumann, default). The right face x=R is the drying surface (Dirichlet or Robin).

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: diameter=6 inches=0.1524 m → radius R=0.0762 m. ASSUMED: strip length 0.01 m (arbitrary — 1D radial problem).

physical_groups.name: axis_symmetry
physical_groups._comment: Left face = axis of symmetry. Default zero-flux Neumann — no BC needed explicitly.

physical_groups.name: drying_surface
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: outer surface of cylinder exposed to RH=0.5. Using Dirichlet h=0.5 (standard approach for mature concrete). Could use Robin moisture film if bp known.

physical_groups.name: top_bottom_sealed
physical_groups._comment: ASSUMED: top/bottom faces sealed (zero flux) — Hanson (1968) specimens sealed at ends during drying. Default Neumann, no explicit BC needed.

points.name: center
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: axis of cylinder (r=0). Used for min-humidity query.

points.name: r_quarter
points._comment: ASSUMED: r = R/4 = 0.0191 m for intermediate profile check.

mesh._comment: ASSUMED: 0.002 m → ~38 elements across the 0.0762 m radius. Adequate for the steep near-surface gradient in Bažant-Najjar S-shape diffusivity. Refine to 0.001 m at surface if needed.

humidity._comment_D0: PAPER_VALUE: C1 = 579×10⁻¹² m²/s = 5.79×10⁻¹⁰ m²/s — explicitly stated in Sec. 7.3.4.1 of Chapter 7 as best-fit for Hanson (1968) data.
humidity._comment_hc: PAPER_VALUE: hc = 0.85 — explicitly stated in Sec. 7.3.4.1.
humidity._comment_n: PAPER_VALUE: N = 3 (paper uses N; pipeline key is n) — explicitly stated in Sec. 7.3.4.1.
humidity._comment_alpha: PAPER_VALUE: a0 = 0.002 — explicitly stated in Sec. 7.3.4.1 as 'alpha' parameter (residual diffusivity ratio at h=0). Note: Chapter 7 calls it a0; pipeline key is 'alpha'. Maps directly.
humidity._comment_capacity: ASSUMED: moisture capacity Ch = 1.0 (dimensionless normalization used in bazant_najjar model; the actual Ch [kg/m³] is absorbed into the diffusivity D(h)). The model solves ∂h/∂t = ∇·(C(h)∇h) with C(h) = D0·[a0 + (1-a0)/(1+((1-h)/(1-hc))^N)]. Capacity=1.0 means no additional storage scaling beyond the S-shape.
humidity._comment_sanity: SANITY CHECK: At h=1 (saturated): C(1)=D0*(a0+1-a0)=D0=5.79e-10 m²/s. At h→0: C(0)=D0*a0=1.16e-12 m²/s. Ratio ≈500× decrease from saturated to dry — consistent with Fig. 7.4 in Chapter 7. Diffusion time scale: τ=R²/D0 = (0.0762)²/(5.79e-10) ≈ 10,030,000 s ≈ 116 days. At 7 days (604800 s) the front has penetrated ~√(D0*t) ≈ √(5.79e-10*604800) ≈ 0.019 m = 25% of radius. Non-linear S-shape will shift this — consistent with Fig. 7.5 showing partial drying at 7 days.

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: cylinder was 7 days old (mature, fully saturated) before drying started at t=0. h=1.0 throughout.

boundary_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: environmental humidity = 0.5 (Sec. 7.3.4.1: 'exposed at 7 days to environmental humidity with 0.5'). Instantaneous Dirichlet is correct here — the cylinder was exposed to a constant RH chamber, not a gradual drying front. No moisture-film Robin BC needed for this controlled lab test.

concrete_domain._comment: No temperature or mechanics. Pure Bažant-Najjar moisture transport only.

time_stepping._comment_t_end: 3 years = 3 × 365 × 86400 s — the LAST of Hanson's four profiles (Fig. 7.5 gives 3 d / 28 d / 180 d / 3 y). Was 604800 (7 d), which reached only the 3-day curve; the other three reference columns fell outside the simulated window entirely.

segments._comment: Very fine at start: steep surface gradient when Dirichlet jumps from 1.0 to 0.5.

dt_strategy._comment: The segment boundaries ARE the four reference times (3 d / 28 d / 180 d / 3 y). That is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a segment end is always an exact grid point, so each results.queries[].at_time lands on a step EXACTLY. With the boundaries elsewhere, at_time fires on the first step past it — the 180-day profile came out 7.5 days late on a plain log grid. 260 steps total.

queries.label: RH at drying surface [-]
queries._comment: Sanity: must equal the Dirichlet value 0.5 at all times.

queries.label: RH radial profile at 3 d
queries._comment: Radial line at mid-height of the strip: axis (r=0) -> drying surface (r=R). 60 samples = 1.3 mm, resolving the near-surface gradient the reference samples at 0/5/10 mm. at_time makes this a SINGLE snapshot (one entry, not a per-step series) — see the dt_strategy comment for why it lands exactly on 3 d.

plots.name: rh_time_history
plots.title: Drying Cylinder — RH Evolution at Gage Points
plots._comment: Time histories only. The Hanson reference curves used to be drawn on this same axes, but they are RH vs distance-from-surface while these are RH vs time — the overlay compared millimetres against days. They now live in rh_radial_profiles.

plots.name: rh_radial_profiles
plots.title: Drying Cylinder — Radial RH Profiles vs Hanson (1968)

curves.label: FEM — 3 d
curves._comment: The query's x column is r [m]; the reference's is (R - r) [mm]. scale_x/offset_x IS that conversion: 76.2 - 1000*r.

curves.label: Hanson — 180 d
curves._comment: ref_id was 'hanson1968_profile_180' (no trailing d) and matched no declared reference_curve, so this curve silently never rendered.

plots._comment: Matching colours pair each FEM profile with its experiment; solid = simulation, dashed+markers = Hanson.

reference_deviation._comment: The references are SPATIAL profiles at four fixed times, not a time series at a point, so the per-step deviation tracker has nothing to track against. Compare visually in rh_radial_profiles (or via VTU/ParaView).
